title: Coefficient pasting for the compositor on fixed compactification models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be any of the coefficient maps specified in [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image]: a homomorphism of finite commutative $\ell$-primary rings, $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_F$ or $E\to F$ for finite $F/E$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, $\mathcal O_E\to E$, $E\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a continuous map $\mathcal O_E\to A$ to a finite admissible ring, or a finite composite. Here $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite and $\mathcal O_E$ its valuation ring; use pulled-back condensed coefficients, including the finite-subextension condensed convention for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Work in ordinary unbounded module-object derived categories on the small pro-étale sites [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Write $T_V=\Lambda'_V\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_V}-$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change], $\gamma_{v,M}:T Rv_*M\to Rv_*TM$ for the unit/pullback/counit comparison [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image], and $\delta_{a,M}:T a_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}a_!TM$ for the canonical open comparison [def-sfb-derived-open-immersion-shriek-iso, det-prop-scalar-six-pullback]. The notation $\Dctf$ means bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

Let $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to S$ have compactifications $c_f=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to Y)$ and $c_g=(i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y,q:\overline Y\to S)$. Choose a dense compactification $(j':\overline X\hookrightarrow W,r:W\to\overline Y)$ of $ip$. All compactifications have the meaning of [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]. Set $H_f=Rp_*j_!$, $H_g=Rq_*i_!$, $H_{gf}=R(qr)_*(j'j)_!$. Define the model compositor
$$\alpha_K:H_gH_fK\xrightarrow{Rq_*\iota_{j_!K}}Rq_*Rr_*j'_!j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{gf}K,$$
where $\iota$ is the identity-on-$Y$ proper/open interchange [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange] and the last arrow is proper direct-image and open-extension composition. This is the canonical compositor on these models. For a model $c=(a,b)$ put $C_{c,M}=Rb_*\delta_{a,M}\circ\gamma_{b,a_!M}$. For every $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ one has
$$C_{(j'j,qr),K}\circ T_S(\alpha_K)
=\alpha_{T_XK}\circ H_g(C_{c_f,K})\circ C_{c_g,H_fK}.$$
Here every functor and compositor on the right after a coefficient comparison is taken over $\Lambda'$. The equality is in $\Dctf(S,\Lambda')$; no comparison between different models of $gf$ is asserted.

proof.text: Put $P=Rp_*$, $Q=Rq_*$, $R=Rr_*$ and $J=j_!$, $I=i_!$, $L=j'_!$; a prime on one of these letters means coefficients $\Lambda'$. Put $A=JK$, $B=J'T_XK$ and $d=\delta_{j,K}:T_{\overline X}A\to B$. By [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images] (2), $A$ is in $\Dctf$, so [lem-sfb-scalar-proper-open-interchange-square] applies to $A$. The same stability clauses (2),(3), and preservation of $\Dctf$ by coefficient change [det-prop-scalar-six-ctf] (3), put all the objects below in the appropriate $\Dctf$. We first calculate in the ambient derived categories. Transport source and target along the canonical proper and open composition identifications used in the definition of $\alpha$. Thus $H_{gf}$ is written $QRLJ$, $\alpha_K$ is $Q(\iota_A)$, and $\alpha_{T_XK}$ is $Q'(\iota_B)$. These are the specified model identifications, with no change of compactification.

source.place: Composition paragraph; explicit pasting on the fixed composite model.

proof.text:
Apply [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image] (2) to $q,r$, and [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (2) to $j',j$. Under the preceding identifications they give
$$\gamma_{qr,LA}=Q'(\gamma_{r,LA})\circ\gamma_{q,RLA},\qquad \delta_{j'j,K}=L'(d)\circ\delta_{j',A}.$$
Consequently the left side of the required identity is
$$E=Q'\bigl(R'L'(d)\circ R'(\delta_{j',A})\circ\gamma_{r,LA}\bigr)\circ\gamma_{q,RLA}\circ T_SQ(\iota_A).$$
In particular these expansions use the proper and open compositors themselves, rather than identifying coefficient comparisons only up to some unspecified isomorphism.

source.place: Composition paragraph; explicit pasting on the fixed composite model.

proof.text:
Naturality of $\gamma_q$ [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image] (2), applied to $\iota_A:IPA\to RLA$, gives
$$\gamma_{q,RLA}\circ T_SQ(\iota_A)=Q'(T_{\overline Y}\iota_A)\circ\gamma_{q,IPA}.$$
Substitute this into $E$ and use functoriality of $Q'$ to obtain
$$E=Q'\bigl(R'L'(d)\circ R'(\delta_{j',A})\circ\gamma_{r,LA}\circ T_{\overline Y}(\iota_A)\bigr)\circ\gamma_{q,IPA}.$$

source.place: Composition paragraph; explicit pasting on the fixed composite model.

proof.text:
The exact interchange coefficient square of [lem-sfb-scalar-proper-open-interchange-square], with input $A=JK$, replaces the middle three factors by
$$R'(\delta_{j',A})\circ\gamma_{r,LA}\circ T_{\overline Y}(\iota_A)=\iota_{T_{\overline X}A}\circ I'(\gamma_{p,A})\circ\delta_{i,PA}.$$
Its hypotheses are exactly the proper $p$, quasi-compact open $i$, and dense compactification $(j',r)$ fixed in the statement; no flatness of the coefficient map is required. Thus
$$E=Q'\bigl(R'L'(d)\circ\iota_{T_{\overline X}A}\circ I'(\gamma_{p,A})\circ\delta_{i,PA}\bigr)\circ\gamma_{q,IPA}.$$

source.place: Composition paragraph; explicit pasting on the fixed composite model.

proof.text:
The natural map $\iota$ in [lem-sfb-scalar-proper-open-interchange-square], now over $\Lambda'$ and evaluated on $d:T_{\overline X}A\to B$, satisfies
$$R'L'(d)\circ\iota_{T_{\overline X}A}=\iota_B\circ I'P'(d).$$
Insert this equality and regroup using functoriality:
$$E=Q'(\iota_B)\circ Q'I'\bigl(P'(d)\circ\gamma_{p,A}\bigr)\circ Q'(\delta_{i,PA})\circ\gamma_{q,IPA}.$$
By the definitions in the statement, the four factors are respectively $\alpha_{T_XK}$, $H'_g(C_{c_f,K})$, and the two factors of $C_{c_g,H_fK}$, since $PA=H_fK$. This is the required right side. Finally $\Dctf(S,\Lambda')$ is a full subcategory of its ambient derived category [sk-def-sfb-constructible], so this equality there is the claimed equality in $\Dctf$.

Each step checks out against the statements it cites. Step 1: ctf-stability (2) applied to j gives A=j_!K in Dctf, which the interchange square needs; ctf (3) covers coefficient change. Step 2: the composition law for gamma (direct-image (2), g=q, f=r) and for delta (pullback (2), j' then j) produce E. Step 3: naturality of gamma_q along iota_A. Step 4: the interchange-square equation matches lem-sfb-scalar-proper-open-interchange-square literally, and its hypotheses hold (p proper, i a quasi-compact open immersion, (j',r) a dense compactification of ip). Step 5: iota is natural over Lambda' because a map out of i_! is determined by its restriction, so marking the step elementary is fine; every listed Lambda' is admissible, so iota exists over it. The regrouping gives exactly alpha_{TK}, H'_g(C_{c_f}) and C_{c_g,H_fK}. Edge cases hold: identity coefficient map, identity opens, identity propers, empty X or K=0, and non-flat maps. There are no new nodes, no duplicates (rg search) and no cycle; the uses of the steps are exactly proof_deps.
